question: How broadly does Bhurloka serve as a place of enjoyment and residence for beings?
premises: Vidyadharas and many other beings are included in Bhurloka.
The text extends the account to the whole creation of beings.
All beings may have places of enjoyment and residence there according to their desire.
inference: Bhurloka functions as a comprehensive world of habitation and enjoyment for the full range of embodied beings.
uncertainties: abhimānato can suggest desire, self-conception, or inclination; 'according to desire' fits the context best.
plain_english: It is also the abode of vidyadharas, and in short, for the whole creation of beings it serves as a place of enjoyment and residence according to their desire.
